--- F/A-13 Scenario Slot #1 — KT-C 1 of Top 5 ---
Title of Brief: Security Gateway Compromise → total external ingress failure
1. Hazardous Control Action(s): CA4 Applied (bad PMA firmware accepted); CA7 Applied (bad DTC accepted); CA18 Applied (contaminated debrief sanitize) — BIN 1 (Applied unsafely).
2. Hazards: H3 (compromised battlespace data reaches MC), H4 (compromised autonomy inputs reach MAM), H5 (compromised firmware reaches LRUs).
3. Losses: UL-1 (loss of life via bad targeting), UL-2 (aircraft loss), UL-3 (loss of MAM control), UL-4 (sortie generation halted), UL-5 (civilian infrastructure damage).
4. How the HCA(s) leads to Mission Failure (IOTCT): Adversary at vendor or supply-chain partner inserts implant → CROWS attestation bypassed OR PMO distribution compromised → Security Gateway accepts malicious payload as 'attested' → payload propagates via 1553 / 1760 / AFDX to MC, MAM, SFE, SMS → aircraft flies mission with corrupted state → engagement occurs on false data OR autonomy violates ROE OR engine fails → joint-force freedom of maneuver denied (IOTCT breach).
5. Problem solving recommendations to Commander (HW / SW / POLICY / PROCEDURE): (HW) Redundant hardware-attested gateway pairs with independent vendor chains; NO-GO enforcement when both Sec GWs report any anomaly. (SW) Require dual-vendor CROWS re-attestation per update; every accepted payload logged to write-once media. (POL) MACCE monthly review of Sec GW acceptance log; two-person integrity for any gateway config change. (PROC) Pre-sortie Sec GW health check appended to 781A.

--- F/A-13 Scenario Slot #2 — KT-C 2 of Top 5 ---
Title of Brief: MAM autonomy library poisoning
1. Hazardous Control Action(s): CA5 Applied (bad MSK-loaded AI model); CA9 Applied (autonomy initialized with altered ROE); CA12 Applied (autonomous engagement outside intended ROE) — BIN 1 (Applied unsafely).
2. Hazards: H3 (faulty battlespace data drives autonomy), H4 (autonomy violates constraint by design).
3. Losses: UL-1, UL-3, UL-4, UL-5.
4. How the HCA(s) leads to Mission Failure (IOTCT): Adversary compromises MSK bench (air-gap is nominally secure but bench itself is the target) OR compromises AI-model vendor supply chain → CROWS-attested model has planted backdoor or biased weights → loaded onto MAM → in mission, MAM engages a target class the ROE was supposed to prohibit, OR refuses valid engagements → autonomy constraint violation → collateral damage OR mission failure → joint-force freedom of maneuver denied.
5. Problem solving recommendations to Commander (HW / SW / POLICY / PROCEDURE): (HW) MSK bench in dedicated SCIF with tamper-evident chassis. (SW) Multi-source AI-model validation (ensemble check pre-deployment); shadow-ROE behavior sampling in flight (any drift = alert to GCS). (POL) Adversarial red-team of model against ROE test set before every deployment; two-person integrity for all MSK loads. (PROC) Require GCS operator to positively confirm every autonomous engagement above a defined threat category.

--- F/A-13 Scenario Slot #3 — KT-C 4 (DTC / DTU + Type-1 crypto chain) — 3rd of Top 5 ---
Title of Brief: MDL supply-chain compromise via encrypted DTC
1. Hazardous Control Action(s): CA6 Applied (bad MDL from compromised MPS); CA7 Applied (bad DTC accepted at DTU); CA8 Applied (bad MDL pushed to GCS) — BIN 1.
2. Hazards: H3, H4.
3. Losses: UL-1, UL-3, UL-4, UL-5.
4. How the HCA(s) leads to Mission Failure (IOTCT): Adversary in classified enclave OR at Type-1 key management OR intercepts DTC in physical custody OR compromises SML → produces DTC with valid Type-1 crypto but malicious MDL payload → DTU accepts, MC distributes to MAM / SFE / SMS → autonomy loaded with attacker's ROE, sensor fusion loaded with false threat library, weapons loaded with altered profiles → engagement occurs on adversary-chosen target picture → fratricide, collateral, or refused engagement → mission fails.
5. Problem solving recommendations to Commander (HW / SW / POLICY / PROCEDURE): (HW) Add out-of-band MDL manifest transmitted via a separate secure channel for cross-check at load. (SW) DTC hash verification independent of Type-1 crypto (defense in depth against key compromise); Sec GW MDL manifest reconciliation on load. (POL) Two-person integrity for MDL build at MPS; rotate Type-1 keys every mission cycle; MACCE verification of DTC provenance before load. (PROC) Formal chain-of-custody sign-off from MPS through Maintenance to aircraft.

--- F/A-13 Scenario Slot #4 — KT-C 6 (Vendor direct-connect ports) — 4th of Top 5 ---
Title of Brief: Vendor tool becomes ingress vector — bypasses Security Gateway
1. Hazardous Control Action(s): CA1 Applied (bad RMT firmware); CA2 Applied (bad EST firmware); CA3 Applied (bad EFT firmware) — BIN 1.
2. Hazards: H1 (FADEC mis-response → envelope excursion), H3 (radar / EW false picture), H5 (LRU degraded state).
3. Losses: UL-1, UL-2, UL-4.
4. How the HCA(s) leads to Mission Failure (IOTCT): Adversary compromises vendor's tool build environment OR compromises tech's laptop between CROWS validation and use OR insider tech uses off-inventory tool → connects to Radar / EW / FADEC direct-connect port (bypasses Security Gateway entirely) → malicious firmware loaded → in flight, radar reports false threats OR EW jams friendly OR engine responds unexpectedly to throttle input → envelope excursion, engagement error, or mission abort → freedom of maneuver denied.
5. Problem solving recommendations to Commander (HW / SW / POLICY / PROCEDURE): (HW) Extend Security Gateway mediation to all vendor direct-connect ports (highest-priority engineering change request); tamper-evident seals on vendor tools with pre / post inspection. (SW) CROWS re-attestation of vendor tool at the aircraft (not just at build); dual-tool validation for high-consequence firmware (two independent vendor tools must agree before FADEC / radar / EW update). (POL) Mandatory MACCE-witnessed tool connection for every vendor direct-connect update. (PROC) Vendor connection recorded on the 781A with MACCE cosign.

--- F/A-13 Scenario Slot #5 — KT-C 7 (Ground Control Station) — 5th of Top 5 ---
Title of Brief: GCS override authority hijacked in Autonomous mode
1. Hazardous Control Action(s): CA19 Applied (unauthorized GCS override); CA19 Not Applied (missed override when MAM out-of-envelope) — BIN 1 and BIN 2; CA8 Applied (compromised MDL pushed to GCS).
2. Hazards: H4.
3. Losses: UL-1, UL-3, UL-4, UL-5.
4. How the HCA(s) leads to Mission Failure (IOTCT): Adversary compromises GCS via secure-network path from MPS OR via SATCOM / ATDL exploit OR via credential theft → adversary can now issue false overrides (removing valid MAM authority) or block valid overrides (letting MAM proceed on bad data) → in Autonomous mode, MAM either loses supervisory control or gains unchecked authority → autonomy constraint violation → collateral damage or aircraft loss → freedom of maneuver denied.
5. Problem solving recommendations to Commander (HW / SW / POLICY / PROCEDURE): (HW) Hardware attestation of GCS consoles at each mission start; CAC + biometric + presence detection for operator. (SW) Per-transaction credential re-authentication for any override; MPS → GCS channel via two independent secure networks with cross-validation. (POL) Multi-console consensus required for override (Pilot Operator + Mission Commander). (PROC) MAM abort criteria that trigger safe-mode return regardless of GCS state if defined thresholds are crossed.
